Subject: Post-demo: throughput & latency notes + next steps

Hi Sophie / Lee —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the two asks I promised to follow up on:

1) Priority & scope
- Primary use case: real-time summarization of customer event logs (avg payload ~380 tokens, worst-case 1.5k).
- Target latency: sub-200ms p95 for 512 token outputs on peak traffic, with predictable bursts.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-range — looking to avoid a 2x surprise vs current endpoint spend.

2) Technical questions we captured (I’ve looped Marissa in for the bench results):
- Expected p95 latency and throughput for 512 token generation on a typical GPU profile.
- What batching / KV-caching improvements look like for your workload shape.
- Quantization impact and compatibility with your compliance needs.

Attachments: I’ll share the short benchmark export and a mutual action plan for next steps.

Suggested next steps:
- Marissa to send numbers from our bench (ETA: EOD Monday) — done/attached when available.
- If numbers look good, 30 min follow-up to review integration plan and a pilot token estimate.

Proposed times: Tue 5/5 10–10:30am PT or Wed 5/6 2–2:30pm PT. If neither works, tell me a good window and I’ll set it.

Thanks —
Dylan

Hi Sophie / Lee —

Thanks for the call. I ran a short, targeted bench on the model variant we discussed (rw-4b-std quantized int8-ish profile) using a 512-token output profile and representative inputs you shared. Notes below — full CSV attached (throughput-summary.csv).

Environment / run details:
- Runtime: Redwood hosted inference (multi-tenant vCPU/GPU pool), 3 runs averaged.
- Typical config used for numbers: no explicit batching (single-request latency), and then a tuned batching run for throughput.

Single-request latency (no batching) — representative numbers:
- p50: ~72 ms (512-token generation, cold KV)
- p90: ~110 ms
- p95: ~145 ms
- p99: ~260 ms

Throughput (batched, batch target 8, continuous batching enabled) — per GPU-equivalent:
- Sustained: ~18–22 requests/sec (512-token) depending on inter-arrival distribution
- Peak burst handling: short bursts to ~35 req/sec with autoscaling/burst buffer

Notes & mitigations:
- KV caching for repeated prefixes (you mentioned many repeated header chunks) reduces per-request compute — expect 20–40% lower latencies for cache-hits.
- Quantization to int8 reduces memory pressure and increases throughput; we left a small headroom for quality (we can run evals on your prompt set).
- If the 1.5k worst-case outputs are in scope, we recommend a different instance class or a sharding approach — expect ~2–3x latency increase at the same batch config for 1.5k tokens vs 512.

Attachments: throughput-summary.csv (contains run-by-run p50/p95/p99 and raw traces), RWI-latency-bench-3x.pdf (short executive summary).

If helpful I can schedule 20 minutes with our infra specialist to walk the runs and trade-offs.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Specialist | Redwood Inference
